context:
Goal: a session can stop a job it started that got stuck, without any risk of stopping someone else's work.
Problem (risk): the guard that stops a session killing processes refuses a session's own stuck job in one case. Allowing it means the guard trusts one more kind of process, which is a safety rule only you change.
Based on (ruling): your rulings Oct 10, 21 and 26: a leftover process counts as the session's own only in two exact cases, listed below.
Based on (measured): Oct 31, Linux: when a stuck job is left behind, the shell that started it loses the session's label, so the guard reads the job as someone else's.
Departs from: the kill guard trusts two kinds of leftover process — b adds a third: a labelled job under a shell that lost its label.

What the "uniform ruling" on option b means: when a shared tool and one case differ, the case changes to fit the tool; the tool does not gain a second accepted form for it. Option b adds a second accepted form to a shared guard, so the page marks it. (The card shows it as t18, a bare id; that is a page fault, now step widens-card-plain-words.)

The timeline:
1. Oct 10, you: a leftover process is the session's own when the machine adopted it and it runs in one of the session's agent folders.
2. Oct 21, you: also when the machine adopted it and it carries the session's label, from the main session only.
3. Oct 26, you: that label rule never applies to an agent, because all agents share one label.
4. Oct 31: a lane's test run got stuck and was left behind. The guards refused every way to wait on it.
5. Oct 31: a lane built a safe way to wait on your own stuck job (bin/wait-pid, #907). It found this gap: waiting is allowed, stopping is not.
6. This question. It has not been asked before; the earlier rulings answered nearby cases.

lastAnswer.note: what was my uniform ruling (t18)? Remember i thought i told claude that it should never just quote a variable to me like that and expect me to understand (Separate mproblem ure doing rn)

options.gain: The kill guard stays as narrow as you ruled it.
options.how: The stop stays refused. The session waits for the job with bin/wait-pid, or the job ends when the session ends.
options.label: Keep today's refusal
options.lose: A stuck job keeps running until it ends or the session ends.

options.gain: The session stops its own stuck job at once.
options.how: From the main session only, a job that carries this session's label counts as its own when the shell above it lost its label.
options.label: Allow stopping a labelled job under a shell that lost its label
options.lose: The guard trusts one more kind of process, so a wrong process number has one more way through.
